claims.text: Encyclopaedia Britannica's account states: "U.S. and Israeli forces launch[ed] Operation Epic Fury" on 28 February 2026, conducting joint strikes on Iran "numbering nearly 900 in just the first 12 hours," and that "Khamenei was killed in the first wave of strikes on February 28, as were dozens of other top Iranian officials," with a strike near Bandar Abbas "killing about 170 people" at a girls' school. Over the following week, "U.S. forces hit about 140 targets with more than 300 strikes."

The same article reports Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes targeting U.S. embassies and military installations 'across the region, including in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Iraq, Oman, and Jordan,' and that 'commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped more than 90 percent after the outbreak of conflict,' with oil prices surging 'from about $70 per barrel just before the war to an average of $103 per barrel in March.'

Encyclopaedia Britannica reports Israel resumed operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon with a ground invasion beginning 17 March 2026, and that this campaign had 'displac[ed] over 1.1 million people by late March.'

Encyclopaedia Britannica reports the memorandum of understanding 'was signed on June 17 by Trump and Iranian Pres. Masoud Pezeshkian,' setting 'a 60-day timeline for an agreement on the unresolved issue of Iran's nuclear program'; the article, last updated 21 August 2026, dates the conflict 'February 28, 2026 - present' and describes hostilities as resumed after Iran struck commercial vessels in July, with the deadline having since lapsed without a permanent settlement.

UNHCR's Operational Data Portal for the Middle East situation records, for movements since 28 February 2026: 568,800 Iranian nationals who have crossed into neighbouring countries (as of 13 August 2026), 245,600 Lebanese refugees (as of 17 August 2026), 352,793 new internally displaced people within Lebanon (as of 10 August 2026), and Afghan and Syrian returnee movements of 848,500 and 849,800 respectively (as of 15 and 17 August 2026).

description: A war between the United States and Israel against Iran and allied forces has continued since 28 February 2026, when nearly 900 US-Israeli strikes in 12 hours killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and dozens of other officials, including a strike near Bandar Abbas that killed about 170 people at a girls' school. Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes on US and allied targets across Jordan, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Iraq and Oman, cutting commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz by more than 90% and pushing oil prices from about $70 to over $100 a barrel. Israel's parallel campaign against Hezbollah in Lebanon has displaced well over a million people; UNHCR now records 568,800 Iranian nationals who have crossed into neighbouring countries and 245,600 Lebanese refugees since the war began, alongside about 1.7 million Afghan and Syrian returnees. A US-Iran memorandum signed 17 June 2026 set a 60-day window to negotiate Iran's nuclear program, but hostilities resumed in July and the deadline expired 17 August 2026 without an agreement, leaving the conflict unresolved.

impact.summary: The opening 28 February strikes killed Iran's Supreme Leader and dozens of officials, and a single strike near Bandar Abbas killed about 170 people at a girls' school; Britannica's running account describes thousands of deaths in Iran and Lebanon and dozens more in Israel and Gulf Arab states, though no single verified cumulative death toll exists. UNHCR's Middle East data portal records, since the war began: 568,800 Iranian nationals who have crossed into neighbouring countries (13 August), 245,600 Lebanese refugees (17 August) and 352,793 new IDPs within Lebanon (10 August) -- a combined 1,167,193 people currently displaced or newly refugees across those two countries -- plus about 1.7 million Afghan and Syrian returnee movements (mid-August). Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz fell more than 90%, and oil prices rose from about $70 to an average of $103 a barrel in March. A June memorandum's 60-day negotiating window for a permanent settlement of Iran's nuclear program expired 17 August 2026 without an agreement, and hostilities remain unresolved.

location.region: Iran, Israel and Lebanon, with strikes and shipping disruption spreading across Jordan, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Iraq, Oman and the Strait of Hormuz

event.scale: Interstate war since 28 February 2026 between the US/Israel and Iran, with strikes and missile/drone exchanges spreading across the Persian Gulf states, Jordan and Lebanon; a June 2026 peace memorandum's 60-day negotiating deadline expired 17 August 2026 without an agreement

name: Iran-Israel-US War
